items.title: The Product Goal Nobody Uses
items.excerpt: Image In Professional Scrum Product Owner training, I ask every class the same question on the second day: describe your Product Goal. Almost everyone can answer. Most have one written down somewhere, on a slide or in a Confluence page, and the room moves on quickly. Then I ask a second question: which items in your current backlog would you remove because they do not contribute to that goal? That question takes longer. The 2020 Scrum Guide added the Product Goal as the commitment for the Product Backlog [1]. Before that revision, teams were expected to have a product direction, but Scrum neve
items.titleJa: プロダクトゴールの使われていない現実

AI has weakened that rationing; the frontier labs need your organization to use more AI with every model generation, and the product operating model promises to fix what Agile supposedly broke. items.titleJa: スクラム実践より重要な5つのプロダクト判断
items.summaryJa: AI時代において、コスト削減のみに注目したプロダクト開発では不十分であり、顧客課題の解決と投資対効果を検証する5つの重要な質問に答えることが必要と主張。プロダクト運用モデルが組織に真の価値をもたらすには、これらの根本的な問いに向き合うべき。

items.title: Beyond the Dam of Knowledge Hoarding
items.excerpt: Picture a developer. Let's call him Chris. Chris has been with the company for twelve years. He knows the billing module better than anyone. When something breaks there, everyone calls him. Documentation? Barely any. Pair programming? Not really his thing. Chris isn't a bad guy. Chris has simply learned how to survive in organizations. If you know something nobody else knows, you're needed. If you're needed, you're safe. For decades, that worked, until AI arrived. It reads the billing module in seconds. items.title: AI generated the user stories – now the real work begins
items.excerpt: AI can generate a list of user stories in seconds. The stories may be clearly written, correctly formatted and connected to recognisable user value. They can give a Product Owner and a whole Scrum Team something concrete to discuss without spending hours facing a blank page. This is genuinely useful – and it is where the more demanding work begins. A well-written user story can still contain an unsupported business rule, an unverified technical assumption or a product decision nobody has made.
